# dripline

> Per-subscriber rate limiting that drips, not floods.
> Fixed-footprint, Redis-optional rate limiting for FastAPI/Starlette/ASGI.
> Zero-dependency core; NumPy and FastAPI behind optional extras. MIT.

## When to use

One machine (or a few), 2–8 ASGI workers, 10^4–10^7 distinct clients, and no
desire to run Redis just for counting. Smaller: a plain dict limiter suffices.
Larger/multi-region exactness: keep Redis at the center.

## Core API (stable arithmetic — sugar lands with the middleware)

```python
from dripline import GcraLimiter

lim = GcraLimiter(rate_per_second=1000 / 60, burst=100)   # 1000/min, bank 100

retry_ns = lim.try_acquire("client-id")   # or pass now_ns= for determinism
retry_ns == 0              # admitted
retry_ns > 0               # rejected: exact wait in nanoseconds

d = lim.try_acquire_decision("client-id")   # explicit pair when preferred
d.allowed, d.retry_after_ns
```

Algorithm: GCRA. One integer per client (earliest admissible time, monotonic
ns). Admit pushes it one interval forward; it may lead the clock by at most
`burst` intervals; rejects are free and return an exact retry hint. No timers,
no cleanup, no resets. The int return keeps the hot path allocation-free —
the largest single measured CPython cost of a tuple-returning API.

## Apex (the flagship: shared arena + tick + presence in one mmap)

```python
from dripline import ApexLimiter

# every worker opens the SAME file: slots, heat map and generation are
# shared — one global budget per client, no Redis, no cleanup thread
lim = ApexLimiter(rate_per_second=1000 / 60, burst=100,
                  slots=1_000_000, path="/run/dripline.apex")
retry_ns = lim.try_acquire("client-id")   # same int contract
```

Three layers in one region (slots | heat map | generation word): L1 answers
"rejected a moment ago" from one byte stamped with the current generation —
rotation is O(1) (bump the generation; old stamps stop matching; writing is
deleting, again). The map bytes are shared, but indices use Python's cached
process-local string hash on purpose — a stable stdlib hash (crc32 + encode)
costs ~2.5x more and a pre-filter must stay cheaper than the path it
fronts; each worker warms its own overlay, so size map_bytes for
workers x rejected clients. L2 locates the client's slot via a stable
fingerprint (same key, same slot, every process). L3 rejects against
a per-process coarse tick (no clock read); L4 admits with a fresh clock —
exact. Measured (4 workers, pinned): 9.4M dec/s = 14% of Rust governor
with TRUE global budgets (admits 301,724 vs 300,000 ceiling) — every
per-worker engine on the same board admits 4x over. Errors are all bounded
and fail-closed: presence false-positives over-reject for at most one
rotation window; a stale tick only makes the limiter stricter; same-slot
races lose at most one update.

## Tick mode (v0.3 — exact admits, clock-amortized rejects)

```python
from dripline import TickGcraLimiter

lim = TickGcraLimiter(rate_per_second=1000 / 60, burst=100, pump_every=512)
retry_ns = lim.try_acquire("client-id")   # same int contract
```

Admits always read a fresh clock (exact); rejects compare against a coarse
shared tick refreshed every `pump_every` decisions. Error direction: a stale
tick is in the past, so pressure only makes the limiter stricter — never
looser; over-rejection is bounded by the pump interval. Measured: 267
ns/dec reject-dominated vs 306 exact / 779 aiolimiter; 10.9M dec/s
multi-worker.

`BloomGcraLimiter` (bloom.py) is experimental: a rotating fail-closed
reject filter that measured SLOWER than the exact path in CPython
(docs/adr/0001) — kept for the mmap-arena-fronting idea, not a shipped
engine.

## Arena API (v0.2 — fixed footprint, shared across workers)

```python
from dripline import ArenaGcraLimiter

lim = ArenaGcraLimiter(rate_per_second=1000 / 60, burst=100,
                       slots=1_000_000)              # 32 MiB, fixed forever
decision = lim.try_acquire("client-id")              # same Decision, same math

# multi-worker: every process opens the SAME file — budgets become global
lim = ArenaGcraLimiter(rate_per_second=1000 / 60, burst=100,
                       slots=1_000_000, path="/run/dripline.arena")

lim.stats()          # occupancy/activity — one NumPy pass (dripline[numpy])
lim.close()          # or use as a context manager
```

Storage: a pre-allocated table of 32-byte slots inside an mmap region — TAT +
stable blake2b fingerprint + two reserved words. Placement is identical in
every process (same key → same slot). Idle clients drain on their own; a
drained slot is indistinguishable from a fresh client, so newcomers recycle
it: RSS never exceeds `slots × 32 bytes` no matter how many clients pass
through. A fixed direct-mapped fingerprint cache keeps the hot path at
hash → one verified slot touch; blake2b runs only on first sight of a key.
Honest bounds: concurrent same-slot writes can lose an update (±1 permit);
an over-subscribed table shares fate at the home bucket — approximate, never
exact.

## Properties

- Workers share one mmap arena (v0.2) — counters are shared, Redis not required.
- Constant memory by construction; "writing is deleting".
- Whole-table maintenance (refill, rollover, metrics, peer merge) = single
  NumPy calls over the arena (`dripline[numpy]`).
- Clock-free mode (v0.3): tick-driven buckets, zero hot-path clock reads,
  guarantees the configured per-window band (e.g. 100–120/min).

## Not

Not planet-scale, not exact under same-client races (±1), not a distributed
consensus system. Honest limitations live in the README.

Docs: README.md (design + roadmap), bench/README.md (measurement rules),
AGENTS.md (build/test/bench commands).
